docs/first-fall-audit-repair.md.text:
# First-fall audit launcher repair

The frozen EXP-PFDR-845d33 package remains an incomplete attempt. This engineering
repair does not overwrite it or grant a research rerun. DEC-20260906-280035 still
requires a separately frozen successor contract.

## Resource and receipt boundary

`tools/audit_process.py` writes `launch.json` before resource setup and retains
stdout, stderr and a terminal `receipt.json` for setup errors, command failures
and timeouts. Output directories are exclusive: a repeated invocation cannot
replace an existing attempt. An externally killed supervisor cannot guarantee a
terminal receipt; its launch record remains available for reconciliation.

On Linux the native backend sets and reads back hard RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_CPU
limits before executing the payload. It records wait4 child CPU and peak RSS.
This backend is for a single-process payload: address-space limits are per
process and are not an aggregate descendant-memory boundary.

On macOS, use the Docker backend with an existing Linux image addressed by its
full `sha256:` image ID. The launcher never pulls a mutable tag. It creates a
container, verifies its configured memory, memory-plus-swap and CPU bounds, then
starts it. The container has swap disabled, one CPU, no network, a read-only
workspace/root filesystem, and a bounded PID count. Docker setup and execution
share the wall budget, with time reserved for forced container cleanup. Cleanup
failure is retained as infrastructure failure. No existing container is removed.

Docker CLI CPU/RSS is not payload telemetry. Docker receipts explicitly leave
those metrics unavailable; an approved successor must collect payload telemetry
inside the container before claiming complete instrument validity. A successfully
exited payload is a process outcome, not a completed-valid research run.

Example (infrastructure probe only; supply a verified local image ID):

```sh
python3 tools/audit_process.py --output /tmp/unique-audit-probe \
  --backend docker --image sha256:FULL_LOCAL_IMAGE_ID --seconds 30 \
  -- python3 -c 'print("probe")'
```

The native backend deliberately refuses macOS instead of replacing a hard memory
limit with an unenforced RSS limit. Host preflight reproduced the original
RLIMIT_AS error, including outside the execution sandbox.

## Manifest compatibility

The JSON schema accepts anchored random-suffix identifiers, an explicit
certificate-kind declaration, and unavailable resource measurements on failed or
inconclusive runs. Completed-valid runs still require numerical resource values.
A claimed mathematical certificate requires `verified: true`. All four existing
normalized failure views now validate without modifying their bytes. The original
manifests still lack the mandatory certificate declaration; their registered
normalized views are the intended schema input.

The supervisor receipt is intentionally not a research manifest. A successor
adapter must construct the canonical manifest and validate it before measurement;
it must not reuse the frozen driver's incompatible extra fields/status layout.

## Definition interface for a successor

A concrete proposed resolution is to form top forms in the ordinary polynomial
ring first and then map them into the truncated ring, preserving each original
generator degree as the weight of its slot in the graded free module. A zero image
then has an explicitly weighted slot, rather than needing an intrinsic degree
assigned to the zero polynomial. The quotient by the declared trivial syzygy
module must use the same weights. Ordinary last-fall computation remains in the
ordinary ring, without adding field equations.

This is a proposed explicit implementation convention, not a new source theorem
or an approved native measurement. The successor must document its agreement with
Definitions 1.3/1.5 and Examples 4.2/4.4 of Caminata–Gorla,
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.05579 (provenance: retrieved in the preceding source audit;
see EXP-PFDR-845d33/source-audit.md and TASK-20260906-46c863's review). In particular,
check the treatment of zero slots against the displayed syzygies before freezing
code. No degree prediction is promoted to an observation by this repair.

## Regression verification

```sh
python3 -m unittest tools.test_audit_process tools.test_audit_manifest_schema -v
```

Tests cover refusal before payload execution, immutable receipts, daemon timeout,
Docker limit readback/cleanup, schema compatibility, and rejection of unsupported
success/certificate claims. Linux integration tests additionally execute a small
successful process, force a wall timeout, and verify an allocation exceeding the
hard address-space limit fails. They are skipped on macOS and run in the dedicated
`audit-runner` GitHub Actions job. These are infrastructure tests, not research
fixture attempts.

experiment:
  id: EXP-PFDR-782085
  hypothesis_id: H-PFDR-232b3a
  version: 1
  title: Exact top-kernel and nonzero-survival panel
  status: review_required
  objective: Test first-layer onset and fall-image dimension separately in a finite correction-aware panel.
  inputs:
    source_idea: IDEA-20260905-e6e2e5
    source_snapshot: 989d62f62
    target_panel:
      candidates:
        - {p: 13, a: 12, b: 3, x_R: 11, s: 2}
        - {p: 19, a: 2, b: 15, x_R: 9, s: 2}
      calibration_grid:
        p: [257,263]
        s: [2,3,4]
        a: 2
        b: 3
        x_R_rule: Least integer x in [0,p-1] for which x^3+a*x+b is a square including zero, checked by exhaustive y enumeration.
    candidate_custody: The two tuples are preregistered replication leads from untracked local review; no untracked code or result is evidence here.
    generator:
      formula: S3=(x1-x2)^2*x_R^2-2*((x1+x2)*(x1*x2+a)+2*b)*x_R+(x1*x2-a)^2-4*b*(x1+x2).
      substitution: x_k=sum(2^i*z_(k,i),i=0..s-1), k=1,2.
      ring: F_p[z_(1,0),...,z_(1,s-1),z_(2,0),...,z_(2,s-1)]/(z_j^2-z_j).
      reduction: Every positive exponent of each variable becomes one.
      formula_source:
        citation: experiments/EXP-PFDR-5726af/run_pfdr_5726af.py
        provenance: internal
        verified_by: codex-root/2026-09-05
  controls:
    - For each target define Q_k=2*sum(2^(i+j)*z_(k,i)*z_(k,j),0<=i<j<s); the curve-free block null is (Q_1+1)*(Q_2+1).
    - For each target the leading-form-only control is H=Q_1*Q_2.
    - Verify both controls have the identical degree-four leading form as the target; do not predict zero falls for H in the Boolean quotient.
    - Exhaustive truth-table evaluation on all 2^(2*s) digit assignments independently checks every constructed polynomial.
  independent_variables:
    - Eight frozen target tuples, with three lower-term variants each.
    - Exact multiplier degree D-4 for D=4,...,2*s+4.
    - All-affine versus rational-target admissibility labels.
  metrics:
    primary:
      - rank(U_D), rank(T_D), dim ker(T_D), and dim U_D(ker T_D).
      - d_layer, the smallest D with a certified nonzero fall image.
    secondary:
      - dim(ker T_D intersect ker U_D), admissibility flags, matrix dimensions, resource use.
  heuristic_under_test: null
  preregistered_prediction:
    quantity: Target first layer and candidate fall dimensions.
    formula: "d_layer=4+floor(s/2); both s=2 candidate tuples predict fall_dim(5)=3, compared with proposed value 4."
    source: IDEA-20260905-e6e2e5; conditional predictions to test, not accepted results.
  scale_relevance:
    tier: toy
    justification: Twenty-four finite polynomial systems with s<=4; no unbounded-family conclusion.
    correspondence: null
  tail_checks:
    - No statistical claim or tail extrapolation; the grid is a deterministic panel.
  replication:
    seeds: [0]
    independent_instances: 0
    labelled_fixture_count: 24
    deduplication: Hash canonical reduced polynomial, field, variable order, and convention. Report 24 labelled fixtures and the actual number of distinct systems; equal systems are not independent replicates.
  protocol:
    admission:
      - Check primality, p>3, 4*a^3+27*b^2 nonzero modulo p, 2^s<=p, and reduced generator degree exactly four.
      - Check rational-target admissibility by exhaustive y enumeration, separately from all-affine membership.
      - Keep a failed admission record and do not replace the tuple.
    maps: >-
      Order squarefree monomials by integer bitmask in the declared variable order.
      The domain at degree D is the span of masks of weight D-4. Column j of U_D
      is the full reduced polynomial z^j*f in the 2^(2*s) mask basis; T_D is its
      projection onto masks of weight D. For D>2*s that projection has zero rows.
      Evaluate every D through 2*s+4 even after the first fall, within the cap.
    certificates: >-
      Use deterministic leftmost-pivot exact Gaussian elimination over F_p.
      Retain matrices, row operations, pivot minors or equivalent rank certificates,
      a basis of ker T_D, and the resulting U_D images. Independently compare
      dim span(U_D(ker T_D)) with rank(U_D)-rank(T_D). The checker reconstructs
      coefficients from the formula using a separate polynomial representation.
    workload: >-
      Sort fixtures by target order (two candidates, then ascending p and s),
      then target/block-null/leading-only. Partition the 24 fixtures into six
      consecutive groups of four, one group per run. Every control and certificate
      check is charged to its run.
    implementation_gate: Retain producer/checker source, exact versions and hashes, and the canonical 24-fixture manifest before measurements.
    theorem_gate: Any Wilson-type top-rank theorem remains an unverified applicability obligation; finite ranks do not discharge a universal theorem or a survival lemma.
  budget:
    wall_clock_seconds_per_run: 1200
    maximum_memory_gb: 8
    total_cpu_hours: 2
    maximum_runs: 6
    maximum_workers: 1
    stages:
      - {name: frozen groups 1 through 3, maximum_runs: 3, wall_clock_seconds: 3600}
      - {name: frozen groups 4 through 6, maximum_runs: 3, wall_clock_seconds: 3600}
    accounting: Six runs sum to 7200 seconds; construction, controls, exact arithmetic, and checking are included.
  stopping_rules:
    - Stop each run at 1200 seconds or 8 GiB and retain every complete and partial degree layer.
    - No additional tuples, replacements, m>=3 cases, or parameter expansion in this version.
    - A missing first fall before a resource stop is right-censored, not absence of a fall.
  invalidation_rules:
    - Incorrect digit reduction, altered lower-term controls, or unidentified generator versions.
    - Inexact rank arithmetic, missing row certificates, or disagreement between the two image-dimension calculations.
    - Using a nonsquare target as a rational-point counterexample.
    - Promoting degree-exhaustion at s=2 as a strict structural early fall.
  receipt_completion_criterion: Every fixture attempt and complete or censored degree profile is retained, including admission failures.
  success_criterion: All blocking controls and decisive target layers complete with independently checked exact maps; the two candidate dimensions and each target onset prediction are separately adjudicated. Missing decisive certificates yield inconclusive.
  falsification_criterion: A certified admissible mismatch refutes only the exact finite prediction or universal formula whose domain contains that fixture. A dimension mismatch alone does not refute the distinct onset law.
  required_artifacts:
    - specification hash and canonical input, control, admission, and deduplication manifests
    - full producer/checker sources with hashes and independent coefficient-reconstruction description
    - exact commands, commit and dirty-tree state, dependency versions, model and verification provenance
    - stdout, stderr, timestamps, resources, and every attempted-run receipt
    - complete U_D and T_D matrices, kernel/image bases, exact rank certificates, and truth-table checks
    - machine-readable degree table separating first layer, image dimension, and target admissibility
  assigned_to: executor
  approved_by: null
  review_requirements:
    - A committed approval and bounded dispatch are required before execution.
    - Precommit a review plan with unique ownership of formula, rank, survival, and domain joints; blind re-derive a candidate matrix from parameters without producer artifacts.
    - Any promoted contradiction or closure requires independent review-breakthrough at max; no downgrade.
  next_decisions:
    positive: If candidate dimensions equal 3 and the predicted target d_layer values are independently verified, separate the finite dimension mismatch from the surviving finite onset prediction and design their distinct proof obligations.
    negative: If candidate predictions fail, preserve the mismatch and inspect the exact polynomial, domain, and map convention.
    inconclusive: Retain incomplete degrees as bounds and rank the cheapest missing certificate before any scale increase.

experiments/EXP-PFDR-25057c/specificatio.text:
experiment:
  id: EXP-PFDR-25057c
  hypothesis_id: H-PFDR-d5f90f
  version: 1
  title: Certified finite increasing-s degree ladder
  status: review_required
  objective: Obtain honest finite degree bounds with complete controls and distinguish growth from censoring and pseudoreplication.
  inputs:
    source_idea: IDEA-20260905-850460
    source_snapshot: 989d62f62
    targets:
      fixed_prime_grid:
        p: 257
        s: [2,3,4]
        curves: [[2,3],[5,7]]
        x_R_rule: Least x in [0,p-1] admitting y^2=x^3+a*x+b, checked by exhaustive y enumeration.
      calibration: {p: 263, s: 2, a: 2, b: 3, x_R_rule: same least-admissible-x rule}
    target_generator: >-
      Use S3=(x1-x2)^2*x_R^2-2*((x1+x2)*(x1*x2+a)+2*b)*x_R+
      (x1*x2-a)^2-4*b*(x1+x2), substitute x_k=sum(2^i*z_(k,i)),
      i=0..s-1, and reduce positive digit exponents to one to obtain f.
    ordinary_system: In the ordinary polynomial ring F_p[z_1,...,z_(2*s)], use the ordered generators f,z_1^2-z_1,...,z_(2*s)^2-z_(2*s).
    quotient_system: The separate layer meter uses f in the Boolean digit quotient and exact-degree squarefree multipliers.
    native_controls: Ordinary F_q[w,x,y,z] with generators x^2-x, x*y-1, w^q-w, w^(q-1)*z^(q-1)-1, for q=3,5; no added equations.
    source:
      citation: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.05579
      provenance: retrieved
      verified_by: codex-root/2026-09-05
      role: Native delayed-fall controls; definition and upper-bound interfaces require checking.
  controls:
    - For each of seven targets use the block null (Q_1+1)*(Q_2+1), where Q_k=2*sum(2^(i+j)*z_(k,i)*z_(k,j),i<j).
    - For each target make a support-matched null by cyclically rotating its nonzero coefficient list by one position separately within each total-degree slice ordered by integer bitmask; preserve exact support, field, variable count, and generator degrees.
    - Native q=3 and q=5 controls must be retained with the same ordinary closure producer and checker.
    - At every native-control prefix below its predicted final fall, the output must remain a bound; a plateau is not terminality.
  independent_variables:
    - s=2,3,4 at fixed p=257 and fixed curve/target-generation rule.
    - p=257 versus 263 at fixed s=2 for the first curve only.
    - Target, block-null, and support-matched-null variants.
  metrics:
    primary:
      - d_layer in the quotient and the certified interval for ordinary d_lf, reported in separate columns.
      - Finite s differences only when both endpoints have sufficient certificates.
      - Completion and correctness of both native delayed-fall controls.
    secondary:
      - Exact closure dimensions, first degree of each lower witness, terminal upper-bound degree, resource use, and distinct input hashes.
  heuristic_under_test: null
  preregistered_prediction:
    quantity: Native ordinary last fall and separate target layer.
    formula: "Native d_lf=5,9 for q=3,5; target d_layer=5,5,6 for s=2,3,4. Ordinary target d_lf has no preregistered numerical value."
    source: Proposal and retrieved native control; no new measurement.
  scale_relevance:
    tier: toy
    justification: Twenty-three labelled deterministic fixtures; fixed finite s and prime grids do not decide asymptotic boundedness.
    correspondence: null
  tail_checks:
    - Report censored endpoints and all attempted layers; do not fit a slope or confidence interval.
    - Repeated deterministic degree values or shared control hashes add no independent samples.
  replication:
    seeds: [0]
    independent_instances: 0
    labelled_fixture_count: 23
    deduplication: Hash canonical polynomial system, field, order, quotient, and convention. Retain duplicates as labelled controls but report the actual distinct count.
  protocol:
    admission: Verify p>3 prime, nonsingular curves, 2^s<=p, rational target admission, and target degree four; retain failures without replacement.
    order: Degree-compatible graded reverse lexicographic with z_1>...>z_(2*s), or w>x>y>z for native controls.
    ordinary_closure: >-
      For D=0,...,D_cap initialize the span of original generators of degree at
      most D. Columns are all ordinary monomials through degree D, ordered by
      descending degree then the declared monomial order. Use exact normalized
      RREF with leftmost pivots. Multiply every degree-at-most-D-1 row by each
      variable in the declared order and repeat reduction until rank stops
      increasing. The degree-filtered row basis spans all low-degree combinations;
      retain row-operation and multiplication derivations. Do not stop the
      across-degree ladder because two consecutive closures have equal dimension.
    lower_certificate: >-
      A witness g of degree less than k with g in V_F,k and g not in V_F,k-1
      certifies d_lf>=k. Retain its positive derivation and an exact rank or
      separating-linear-functional certificate for nonmembership.
    upper_certificate: >-
      At each completed D test the nonzero closure rows as a candidate Gröbner
      basis of the original ideal, using all Buchberger pairs in lexicographic
      row-index order and deterministic least-index division. Check both ideal
      inclusions and certify every basis row in V_F,D. Retain the
      degree-compatible division proof that this implies d_lf<=D. This proof is
      an explicit applicability prerequisite, not an asserted result of this
      design. If it is unverified, publish only the certified lower bound.
    exactness: >-
      Report an exact ordinary last-fall value only when the maximum certified
      lower bound equals a certified upper bound. Otherwise report [L,U] with
      null U when no upper certificate exists. No output-basis degree is used as
      last fall. Solving-degree measurement is outside this version.
    layer_meter: >-
      Separately form U_D from all squarefree multipliers of weight D-4 times f
      in the quotient, and T_D from its degree-D rows, for D=4,...,2*s+4.
      d_layer is the first D with rank(U_D)-rank(T_D)>0, with exact certificates.
      No equality or gap with ordinary d_lf is interpreted without a transfer proof.
    caps:
      ordinary_degree: D_cap=2*s+4 for targets and their nulls; D_cap=10 for native controls.
      maximum_matrix_columns: 20000
      maximum_matrix_entries: 25000000
      cap_action: Refuse the next matrix, retain the current bounds, and report resource censoring.
    scheduling: >-
      Order the two native controls first, followed by targets sorted by p,s,a,b,
      each followed by block null and support-matched null. Split the 23 fixtures
      into 12 consecutive groups of at most two. Every attempted construction,
      checker, and control is charged to its group; no fixture replacement.
    retention_gate: Freeze and retain all producer/checker source and hashes, canonical inputs, dependency versions, and exact commands before measuring any target.
  budget:
    wall_clock_seconds_per_run: 1200
    maximum_memory_gb: 8
    total_cpu_hours: 4
    maximum_runs: 12
    maximum_workers: 1
    stages:
      - {name: native blocking controls, maximum_runs: 1, wall_clock_seconds: 1200}
      - {name: target and null groups, maximum_runs: 11, wall_clock_seconds: 13200}
    accounting: Twelve sequential groups total 14400 seconds; all checking and partial attempts are included.
  stopping_rules:
    - Stop each group at 1200 seconds, 8 GiB, its degree cap, or a matrix cap; retain bounds and censoring.
    - A failed native control blocks target-degree interpretation; remaining attempted records may be retained without a scientific conclusion.
    - No additional primes, larger s, fitted extrapolation, or unbounded-family search.
  invalidation_rules:
    - Missing producer or checker source for any blocking control.
    - Conflated ordinary and quotient degree conventions or unverified reduction interfaces.
    - Uncertified exact last-fall value, inexact arithmetic, lost attempts, or altered fixture generation.
    - Treating deterministic repeated degrees as independent statistical evidence.
  receipt_completion_criterion: Retain the manifest and every attempted or unattempted fixture with its completion, invalidity, or censoring reason.
  success_criterion: Both native controls certify their predicted last falls; target layer predictions and every reported finite ordinary difference have all endpoint certificates and matching control records. Missing decisive certificates yield inconclusive.
  falsification_criterion: A fully certified finite mismatch refutes only its declared prediction; an invalid exactness or sample-independence assertion refutes the instrument claim. Censoring refutes neither mathematical claim.
  required_artifacts:
    - specification hash, complete fixture/control manifests, and admission/deduplication table
    - all producer/checker sources and hashes, commands, commit/dirty state, environment/dependency and model provenance
    - stdout, stderr, timestamps, resources, and every attempted or omitted fixture receipt
    - ordinary closure matrices and derivations, witness/nonmembership and Gröbner certificates, upper-bound applicability note
    - separate quotient-layer matrices/rank certificates and machine-readable interval/censoring table
    - report with fixed-prime s differences separated from fixed-s prime calibration
  assigned_to: executor
  approved_by: null
  review_requirements:
    - Execution requires a committed approval and bounded dispatch.
    - Before a claim-changing round, commit prior, unique owners for closure/lower/upper/interface joints, blindness, a known-false truncation control, and a blind re-derivation excluding producer artifacts.
    - A proposed contradiction, closure, or asymptotic statement requires independent review-breakthrough at max without degradation.
  next_decisions:
    positive: Independently verify certified finite differences, then rank a separate unbounded-family proof obligation if they warrant one.
    negative: If certified degrees fail the finite prediction, isolate the parameter/convention mismatch and preserve the result.
    inconclusive: Retain bounds and identify the cheapest missing terminality or control certificate; do not increase scale automatically.

ledger/hypotheses/H-PFDR-232b3a.yaml.text:
hypothesis:
  id: H-PFDR-232b3a
  question_id: RQ-PFDR-ae2fba
  source_idea_id: IDEA-20260905-e6e2e5
  title: Separate top-kernel onset from nonzero survival in the prime-digit first fall
  statement: >-
    For the specified m=2 digit systems, the finite preregistered prediction is
    d_layer=4+floor(s/2), while the dimension of the fall space requires
    a separate survival and independence calculation. The two frozen candidate
    tuples predict dimension 3 rather than the previously proposed 4 at degree 5.
  mechanism: >-
    For exact squarefree multipliers of degree D-4, construct the full reduced
    product map U_D and its degree-D projection T_D. The nonzero fall image is
    U_D(ker T_D), with dimension rank(U_D)-rank(T_D). A top-kernel vector that
    maps to zero under U_D contributes no nonzero fall.
  assumptions:
    - Odd prime field, nonsingular short Weierstrass coefficients, m=2, and 2^s<=p.
    - Boolean digit quotient and exact-degree multiplier layer are fixed definitions.
    - All-affine and rational-point target domains are reported independently.
    - Top-rank and survival conditions require proof before any universal law is claimed.
  proof_search_map:
    bottleneck: A top-kernel count does not alone determine nonzero fall dimension.
    baseline_embedding:
      parameter_slice: s=2,3,4 with the frozen prime-digit generator and its degree-four leading form.
      reproduction_check: Reconstruct products from the explicit S3 polynomial and verify exact ranks.
    observation_collision:
      observable: The top map T_D and its kernel dimension.
      distinct_preimage_search: Hold T_D fixed while replacing lower terms with a block null or zero.
    constructive_transforms:
      - transform: stronger_invariant
        proposed_object: The full map on the top kernel and its certified image dimension.
        predicted_gain: Detect a one-dimension survival deficit even when first-fall onset is unchanged.
    quantifier_order: >-
      Each certificate concerns one frozen tuple and convention. One admissible
      mismatch refutes a universal dimension formula on its exact domain; it does
      not refute the distinct first-fall law. Passing a finite panel proves neither
      universal law nor generic probability statement.
    method_ceiling:
      strongest_certifiable_claim: Exact finite ranks, fall dimensions, and first nonzero layer in 24 systems.
      nearby_object_control: Identical leading form with two different lower-term rules.
    proof_obligations:
      - claim: The full and top maps implement the frozen squarefree layer.
        responsibility: correctness
      - claim: The rank difference equals the image of the top kernel.
        responsibility: interface
      - claim: Every claimed counterexample satisfies its asserted target domain.
        responsibility: scope
      - claim: Any top-rank theorem and nonzero-survival statement have separate applicability proofs.
        responsibility: strictness
    not_applicable_reason: null
  asymptotic_claim: null
  heuristic_assumptions: []
  structural_ingredients:
    - description: Prior prime-digit generator and layer convention, used as a reconstruction input.
      citation: experiments/EXP-PFDR-5726af/run_pfdr_5726af.py
      provenance: internal
      verified_by: codex-root/2026-09-05
      role: Formula reference; no historical observation is adopted as a new result.
  predictions:
    - metric: First nonzero target layer.
      direction: different
      minimum_effect: Preregistered d_layer values 5,5,6 at s=2,3,4.
    - metric: Degree-five fall dimension for the two candidate tuples.
      direction: lower
      minimum_effect: Predicted 3 versus proposed universal value 4; replication required.
  test_boundary:
    instances:
      - Eight target systems, each with block-null and leading-form-only controls.
    parameters:
      m: 2
      s: [2,3,4]
      base_primes: [257,263]
      candidate_tuples: [[13,12,3,11],[19,2,15,9]]
    implementation: Independent exact polynomial expansion and modular rank certificates.
    budget:
      maximum_runs: 6
      wall_clock_seconds_per_run: 1200
      maximum_memory_gb: 8
      total_cpu_hours: 2
  falsification_conditions:
    - A certified admissible target first-fall value differs from 4+floor(s/2).
    - A candidate dimension prediction fails exact reconstruction.
  interpretation_limits:
    - The candidate tuples are untracked review leads, not accepted evidence.
    - s=2 has degree-exhaustion effects and is not evidence of a strict early fall.
    - Binary Weil-descent degree bounds do not automatically transfer to this prime-digit quotient.
    - No claim concerning m>=3, asymptotic bounded degree, or end-to-end ECDLP complexity.
  status: specified
  proposed_by: coordinator

ledger/hypotheses/H-PFDR-d5f90f.yaml.text:
hypothesis:
  id: H-PFDR-d5f90f
  question_id: RQ-PFDR-ae2fba
  source_idea_id: IDEA-20260905-850460
  title: Certified finite degree-growth ladder with blocking controls
  statement: >-
    A finite increasing-s ladder with retained producers, separate degree
    conventions, and two-sided last-fall certificates can distinguish an actual
    degree increase from a censoring or replication artifact. The native
    separation controls should be certified, while target layer values are
    predicted to change from 5 at s=2 to 6 at s=4. No ordinary last-fall value is
    predicted before its certificate exists.
  mechanism: >-
    Compute the quotient generator-layer profile and an explicitly separate
    ordinary-ideal closure ladder. Retain witnesses for lower bounds and a
    checked Gröbner-basis containment/division argument for upper bounds. Compare
    changing s at fixed prime separately from fixed-s prime calibration.
  assumptions:
    - Exact finite-field arithmetic and complete retained source for every blocking control.
    - Ordinary-ring and quotient-layer invariants have separate names and no inferred equality.
    - A plateau or a largest output-basis degree does not certify last-fall completion.
  proof_search_map:
    bottleneck: Incomplete degree ladders and repeated deterministic values can imitate degree evidence.
    baseline_embedding:
      parameter_slice: Native ordinary separation controls at q=3 and q=5 and quotient targets at s=2.
      reproduction_check: Certify native last-fall values 5 and 9 and retain every required source and certificate.
    observation_collision:
      observable: An apparently stable degree table or repeated deterministic degree.
      distinct_preimage_search: Compare truncation before a known delayed fall and repeated hashes against genuinely distinct parameter rows.
    constructive_transforms:
      - transform: stronger_invariant
        proposed_object: A certified interval with its witness, terminality proof, convention, and censoring marker.
        predicted_gain: Eliminate false exact values and false sample-size inflation in the frozen panel.
    quantifier_order: >-
      The finite differences belong only to the fixed-prime s=2,3,4 panel.
      Even positive differences cannot refute an unspecified O(1) bound.
      A future unbounded-family claim must quantify all s and prove a growing
      lower bound with every representation interface stated.
    method_ceiling:
      strongest_certifiable_claim: Finite degree bounds and differences where both endpoints are certified.
      nearby_object_control: Native delayed-fall fixtures must remain censored below their known final fall.
    proof_obligations:
      - claim: Each V_F,D is the full degree-filtered multiplication closure.
        responsibility: correctness
      - claim: Checked Gröbner containment and degree-compatible division give the stated upper bound.
        responsibility: interface
      - claim: A lower witness lies outside the previous closure but inside the current one.
        responsibility: strictness
      - claim: Ordinary and quotient labels are never transferred without a separate proof.
        responsibility: scope
      - claim: Control generation, checking, and incomplete attempts are charged to the resource budget.
        responsibility: runtime
    not_applicable_reason: null
  asymptotic_claim: null
  heuristic_assumptions: []
  structural_ingredients:
    - description: Native closure definitions and separation controls.
      citation: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.05579
      provenance: retrieved
      verified_by: codex-root/2026-09-05
      role: Blocking controls and source-interface audit.
    - description: Iterated V_F,D framework with explicit scope conditions.
      citation: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1505.02532
      provenance: retrieved
      verified_by: codex-root/2026-09-05
      role: Definition reference; no automatic prime-digit theorem.
  predictions:
    - metric: Native-control last-fall certificate intervals.
      direction: different
      minimum_effect: Exact [5,5] and [9,9] if completed; premature truncation must remain censored.
    - metric: Target generator-layer difference from s=2 to s=4 at fixed prime.
      direction: higher
      minimum_effect: Preregistered increase of one, from 5 to 6; separate from ordinary last fall.
  test_boundary:
    instances:
      - Seven target systems, each with two matched controls.
      - Two native ordinary-ring delayed-fall controls.
    parameters:
      fixed_prime: 257
      s: [2,3,4]
      fixed_s_prime_calibration: {s: 2, p: 263}
      native_q: [3,5]
    implementation: Exact degree-filtered ordinary closure plus separately named quotient-layer meter.
    budget:
      maximum_runs: 12
      wall_clock_seconds_per_run: 1200
      maximum_memory_gb: 8
      total_cpu_hours: 4
  falsification_conditions:
    - A certified native control or target layer value contradicts its finite prediction.
    - The instrument reports exact last fall without matching certificates or treats repeated hashes as independent observations.
  interpretation_limits:
    - Missing control sources or incomplete bounds prevent the affected comparison.
    - Equal first and last degree values can coexist with growth; equality does not establish bounded degree.
    - No slope confidence intervals, asymptotic disproof, relation yield, or ECDLP complexity claim.
  status: specified
  proposed_by: coordinator

    guard and failure-capture preflight that records launch failure before

  target_ids: [EXP-PFDR-a76b91, BATCH-ff2730]

    the approval DEC-20260907-c9b61c and the re-filed user authorization

    predecessor disposition DEC-20260906-280035 (incomplete attempt, zero of
    eight fixtures measured) is superseded operationally by this run, not

    predecessor's arithmetic still blocks it, exactly as the frozen protocol
    prescribes.

  target_ids: [EXP-PFDR-a76b91, H-PFDR-2139a5]
  rationale: >-
    The contract's own success_criterion governs: "All eight decisions
    complete correctly, both native controls have the certificates required by
    the finite claims, and no invalid claim is accepted. Missing decisive
    certificates yield inconclusive." The native degree controls (groups 1 and
    3) carry no certificates because the Definition 1.3 / Example 4.4
    zero-slot grading interface remains unresolved, exactly as the frozen
    protocol prescribes for an unresolved interface (group 1 procedure: "If
    that interface is unresolved, record unmeasured"; stopping rule 2: "Stop
    arithmetic on an unresolved native-definition interface; metadata fixtures
    may still complete"). The measured component - zero invalid acceptances,
    checker-verified, 8 of 8 fixtures - is recorded as instrument-level
    evidence in EV-PFDR-55d067 but does not by itself satisfy the success
    criterion, which also requires the native controls to carry the
    certificates the finite claims depend on. The decision is therefore
    inconclusive, per the contract's next_decisions.inconclusive branch:
    retain the unresolved interface and design its cheapest certificate
    prerequisite.

    - source: experiments/EXP-PFDR-a76b91/execution-report.yaml

    - source: experiments/EXP-PFDR-a76b91/runs/RUN-PFDR-20260907-d934ea/

      provenance: internal
      access_note: Group 4 (quantifier and domain controls) canonical run record; rejected_inference and inadmissible as designed.
    - source: DEC-20260906-280035
      provenance: internal
      access_note: The predecessor disposition this run supersedes operationally, not scientifically.
    - source: DEC-20260907-c9b61c
      provenance: internal
      access_note: The approval of this frozen successor contract.
  limitations:
    - The native Definition 1.3 / Example 4.4 zero-slot grading interface remains unresolved; groups 1 and 3 are unmeasured by design and no degree estimate was substituted.
    - Single experiment, single seed (0), zero independent instances; eight deterministic toy fixtures, not a sample.
    - Toy scale throughout (q in {3,5}; the F_19 enumeration is a declared control, not a scale claim).
    - The payload interpreter is container CPython 3.10.12; the host interpreter is not the payload interpreter.
    - The checker is a separate implementation from the same Executor session (independent_session: false per the manifests' own note); it is not independent research validation.
    - This decision changes no hypothesis status, no goal status, and no claim tier; no promotion of any degree prediction; the survival panel remains unauthorized.

Neither affects the validity or the disposition of the four runs.

experiments/EXP-PFDR-a76b91/source-audit.text:
# Source-definition audit

Retrieved directly by Executor via web tool on 2026-09-06: Caminata and Gorla, arXiv:2112.05579v2, 1 June 2022, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.05579 . Provenance: retrieved. Locations read: Definition 1.3 (printed page 5), Definition 1.5 (page 6), Theorem 3.1 proof (page 11), Example 4.4 (pages 13–14).

Native first fall uses syzygies of top forms in B=F_q[w,x,y,z]/(w^q,x^q,y^q,z^q), modulo the module generated by Koszul vectors and f_i^(q-1)e_i. Its grading uses deg(b_i)+deg(f_i). Ordinary last fall uses iterated V spaces in R; Theorem 3.1 requires a degree-compatible order.

UNRESOLVED INTERFACE: Example 4.4 includes w^q among top forms although it is zero in B. The retrieved definition does not explicitly grade that zero generator, state whether to retain its prequotient degree, or reconcile taking top forms before/after passage to B. Retaining original slot weights is plausible but is not assumed here. This is an implementation prerequisite unresolved by this Executor, not a defect or contradiction established in the paper.

The frozen stopping rule therefore stops all native arithmetic. No native matrices, first/last-fall bounds, Groebner certificates, or solving-degree bounds are produced. Predictions (3,5,5) and (3,9,9) remain source controls, never observations. Dependent finite claims are inconclusive. Metadata fixtures and the separately declared rational-target enumeration remain executable. Revisit requires a documented resolution of this precise interface under appropriate Coordinator authority.

primary_reading.summary: Native first fall uses syzygies modulo trivial syzygies in a truncated homogeneous ring. Last fall uses ordinary-ring multiplication-closed spaces V. Degree-compatible Groebner bases connect those spaces to last-fall upper bounds. Example4.4 gives ordinary last fall2q-1, hence5 and9 for q3 and5. Example4.2 explicitly drops a zero top-form when displaying nontrivial syzygies. No zero-slot convention for all systems is adopted by this reading.

retrieval_limit: collection 'crypto_knowledge_v1' does not exist in this process. CRYPTO_KB_QDRANT_URL is ':memory:', which is an embedded index that lives and dies with the process -- ingesting in one command and searching in another cannot work. Either point at a server (`make qdrant-up`, then CRYPTO_KB_QDRANT_URL=http://localhost:6333) or use a file-backed embedded index (CRYPTO_KB_QDRANT_URL=./.kb-index), then re-run `crypto-kb ingest`.
